prompt: Pixel art in the style of a 1984 home-computer title screen, 16-colour palette, crisp square pixels with no anti-aliasing. Two phones lie face up on a deep indigo field, each screen glowing a different mood colour, one calm blue, one hyped red. Between them, square waves, triangle waves and sine waves drawn as chunky pixel lines rise and braid together like a music staff, with small square notes riding the lines in eight colours: blue, red, purple, yellow, green, grey-violet, orange, indigo. A thick light-purple screen border frames the scene. No words, no logos, no real brands.

A warm photograph of a small vintage green-phosphor oscilloscope on a wooden workbench in late afternoon California light, its round screen showing a crisp narrow pulse wave beside a smooth triangle wave. A modern smartphone leans against it, its screen a deep blue with a single row of coloured square buttons. Shallow depth of field, solder spool and a pair of earbuds nearby. No brand names, no logos, no readable text anywhere.
